content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., sentiment > 0.33) — reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon post-spike.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.33 or below), model fails to correct downward — apply downward bias of 2–5% for 30d horizon if sentiment drops sharply.
- Forecast shows strong upward momentum but true price often reverses within 5–7 days — introduce mean reversion rule: if forecast > 95% of recent 7-day high, reduce by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- Model ignores sentiment decay — if sentiment drops from 1.00 to 0.00 within 3 days, reduce forecast slope by 50% for next 7 days.
- For 30d horizon, if true price drops below 90% of 30d forecast mean, apply “lag correction”: subtract 1–3% per day until price stabilizes or sentiment rebounds.
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., forecast 95+ vs true 90–95) is common — cap forecast at 95% of 30d high if sentiment is positive and price has already peaked.
